notes:
Getting GAMbit working again now: download the latest GAMbit-Setup .exe from your GitHub Releases page and run it, choosing “only for me” again. Your settings and schedules live separately from the program files, so they should all still be there. Then build and publish this version so the next update can’t do the same thing.

1. The update broke GAMbit

Most likely cause: the installer deleted GAMbit’s program files before copying the new ones. If any copy of GAMbit was still running, including a scheduled background job, the copy failed partway and nothing put the old files back. That leaves an install that won’t open.
What the installer does now:
Closes every running GAMbit, including background jobs.
Moves the old files aside instead of deleting them, then copies the new version.
Deletes the old files only after the install succeeds, and puts them back if it doesn’t.
Other safeguards:
Updates now install to the same place as your existing install, so a “just me” install stays “just me”.
Background jobs skip their run while an update is installing.
Each update writes a log to %TEMP%\GAMbit-update.log. If anything goes wrong, send me that file.

2. Schedules showed only one of your two tasks

Cause: to get the task list, GAMbit asked Windows for every scheduled task on the PC. On many PCs that fails with “Access is denied” because of protected system tasks, and GAMbit then threw away the whole list. Only saved jobs, which GAMbit keeps itself, still showed.
Fix: it now asks only for GAMbit’s own tasks, so every one should appear, with its real time, days and on/off state.
Missing tasks are flagged: a saved job whose Windows task has gone shows “⚠ not in Task Scheduler”. Opening it and clicking Save re-creates it.
Lost-job bug fixed: a background job finishing at the same moment you created a new job could wipe out the new one. That can’t happen now.

3. Home → Background jobs

When you open GAMbit, it lists what ran since you were last in. It covers at least the last 24 hours, so after a weekend it shows everything since Friday.
Each job is marked ✔ succeeded, ✖ failed (with the reason), or ⚠ didn’t run. “Didn’t run” means a saved job was due but never started, for example because the PC was off or you were signed out.
Order: failures come first. Double-click a row for its log, or use Last 7 days for a wider view.
Starts empty: results are only recorded from this version on, so the list fills in from the first run after you install it.
